title: Stock market warning: Waning buybacks a warning for S&P 500 firms
excerpt: Buybacks are down in sectors like tech and communications, a sign that companies aren't in a position to repurchase their stock like they used to.
content_html:
Why dwindling buybacks are a warning for stocks

By Jennifer Sor

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Companies aren't buying back their stock like they used to, and that's a potential warning sign for the market, Ned Davis Research says.

The research firm flagged waning stock buybacks among S&P 500 companies in the first quarter — a possible sign that some firms in the benchmark index aren't in a position to shell out and return money to investors.

Net stock buybacks in 2025 surpassed $1 trillion in each quarter, though repurchase agreements slipped slightly below the $1 trillion mark in the first quarter of this year, NDR said, citing its analysis of S&P data.

Overall, stock repurchases in the benchmark index remain near records, but activity is weaker in specific sectors of the market.

Communications, an area in which firms have been eager to buy back their own stock, has seen a "steep drop off" in repurchase agreements the last two quarters, NDR said, with net repurchases falling to around $186 billion in the first quarter, down from a recent peak of over $230 billion.

Tech, another area where stock buybacks have boomed in recent years, has also seen repurchase activity stall, with net buybacks declining to $250 billion in the first quarter, down from their recent peak of over $260 billion.

"Aggregate buyback data hides the fact that a growing percentage of companies are not in as strong of a position to repurchase their own stock as they have been for much of the past decade," the firm wrote, pointing to the discrepancy between buyback data for the broader index and individual sectors.

More investors are on guard and bracing for broader market turbulence, particularly as volatility rips through the AI sector this summer.

Concerns have also been rising in particular about the financial health of some AI giants, who have doubled down on their capex spending despite monetization plans remaining in the early stages for many.

Goldman Sachs wrote earlier this year that colossal capex was coming at the expense of buybacks, with the decline in repurchases largely concentrated in the tech sector.

Capex spending at Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon — four of the biggest AI spenders on Wall Street — is on track to grow 77% this year, according to an estimate from the veteran tech investor Gene Munster.

Spending is also being funded increasingly with debt. Among Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle, incremental annual debt as a percentage of capex has climbed from 9% to 32% since 2024, according to a recent FactSet analysis.

Free cash flow is expected to move "close to zero or turn negative" at Amazon, Meta, and Oracle this fiscal year, the firm added.

content_html_zh:
为什么回购减少是对股票的警告

作者：Jennifer Sor 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

内德戴维斯研究公司表示，公司不再像以前那样回购股票，这对市场来说是一个潜在的警告信号。

该研究公司指出，第一季度标准普尔 500 指数公司的股票回购量正在减少，这可能表明基准指数中的一些公司无法向投资者支付和返还资金。

NDR 援引对标准普尔数据的分析表示，尽管今年第一季度回购协议略低于 1 万亿美元大关，但 2025 年每个季度的股票净回购额均超过 1 万亿美元。

总体而言，基准指数的股票回购仍接近历史记录，但市场特定板块的活动较弱。

NDR 表示，通信领域的公司一直渴望回购自己的股票，但过去两个季度的回购协议“急剧下降”，第一季度净回购额降至 1860 亿美元左右，低于近期超过 2300 亿美元的峰值。

科技股是近年来股票回购蓬勃发展的另一个领域，但回购活动也陷入停滞，第一季度净回购额从近期超过 2600 亿美元的峰值降至 2500 亿美元。

该公司写道：“总体回购数据掩盖了这样一个事实，即越来越多的公司没有像过去十年的大部分时间那样强大地回购自己的股票。”他指出了更广泛的指数和个别行业的回购数据之间的差异。

越来越多的投资者保持警惕，准备应对更广泛的市场动荡，尤其是今年夏天人工智能行业出现波动。

人们对一些人工智能巨头的财务状况的担忧也在不断增加，尽管许多公司的货币化计划仍处于早期阶段，但这些巨头的资本支出却翻了一番。

高盛今年早些时候写道，巨额资本支出是以回购为代价的，回购的下降主要集中在科技行业。

根据资深科技投资者吉恩·蒙斯特 (Gene Munster) 的估计，Alphabet、Meta、微软和亚马逊这四家华尔街最大的人工智能支出公司的资本支出今年有望增长 77%。

支出也越来越多地通过债务融资。 根据最近的 FactSet 分析，自 2024 年以来，Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta、微软和甲骨文的年度债务增量占资本支出的比例已从 9% 攀升至 32%。

该公司补充称，亚马逊、Meta 和甲骨文本财年的自由现金流预计将“接近于零或变为负值”。
